Jollof Rice with Chicken

55 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Frying the Tomato-Pepper Base

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Chicken thighs, bone-in skin-on150g300g450g600g
Long-grain parboiled rice75g150g225g300g
Plum tomatoes, fresh or canned60g120g180g240g
Red bell pepper (tatashe)30g60g90g120g
Scotch bonnet pepper¼½¾1
Onion, divided30g60g90g120g
Vegetable oil15ml30ml45ml60ml
Tomato paste10g20g30g40g
Garlic cloves, minced1234
Fresh ginger, grated½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Curry powder¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Dried thyme¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Bay leaf¼½¾1
Chicken stock90ml180ml270ml360ml
Bouillon cube¼½¾1
Salt¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp

Steps

  1. Season the chicken thighs with salt, a pinch of curry powder, thyme, half the garlic, and half the ginger. Set aside.
  2. Blend the tomatoes, red bell pepper, scotch bonnet, and half the onion (roughly chopped) into a smooth puree.
  3. Ask an adult to help heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken thighs on both sides, about 4 minutes per side, then remove and set aside.
  4. In the same pot, sauté the remaining onion (sliced) until soft, then stir in the tomato paste and fry 2 minutes.
  5. Pour in the blended tomato-pepper puree. Fry over medium heat, stirring often, for 15–20 minutes until it thickens, darkens, and the oil visibly separates and rises to the top — this step is what gives real jollof its depth.
  6. Stir in the remaining curry powder, thyme, bay leaf, bouillon cube, and stock. Return the chicken and simmer 15 minutes, until cooked through.
  7. Lift the chicken onto a plate. Stir the rice into the sauce so every grain is coated; the liquid should just barely cover the rice.
  8. Cover tightly (foil under the lid helps seal in steam) and cook over low heat 20–25 minutes without lifting the lid, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed. Letting the very bottom catch slightly gives the classic smoky flavor.
  9. Nestle the chicken back on top to reheat, fluff the rice gently with a fork, and serve.

Egusi Soup

55 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Grinding the Egusi Seeds

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Goat meat or beef, cubed100g200g300g400g
Ground egusi (melon seeds)60g120g180g240g
Red palm oil20ml40ml60ml80ml
Onion, chopped20g40g60g80g
Plum tomato/pepper, blended30g60g90g120g
Scotch bonnet pepper¼½¾1
Ground crayfish, optional½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Dried fish or stockfish, optional15g30g45g60g
Stock or water120ml240ml360ml480ml
Fresh spinach, chopped40g80g120g160g
Bouillon cube¼½¾1
Salt¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp

Steps

  1. Season the meat with a little chopped onion, salt, and the bouillon cube. Ask an adult to help boil it in water to cover until tender, 25–35 minutes. Reserve the cooking stock.
  2. Mix the ground egusi with a splash of water or reserved stock to form a thick, scoopable paste.
  3. Heat the palm oil in a pot over medium heat, add the remaining onion, and sauté until soft.
  4. Stir in the blended tomato and scotch bonnet, and fry 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
  5. Drop spoonfuls of the egusi paste into the pot, or stir it in smooth if you prefer — let it fry gently in the oil for 5 minutes to toast without burning.
  6. Gradually pour in the reserved meat stock, stirring to loosen the egusi into a thick soup. Add the cooked meat, crayfish, and dried fish if using.
  7. Simmer uncovered 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the egusi is fully cooked and a layer of oil floats on top.
  8. Stir in the chopped spinach and simmer 5 more minutes until just wilted. Adjust salt to taste and serve hot with rice or pounded yam.

Suya

25 min (+15–30 min rest)EasyServes 1–4

Prep — Coating Skewers in Yaji Spice

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Beef sirloin or flank steak, thinly sliced150g300g450g600g
Roasted peanuts, ground30g60g90g120g
Cayenne pepper½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Paprika½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Ground ginger¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Garlic powder¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Onion powder¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Ground clovespinch⅛ tsp¼ tsp¼ tsp
Bouillon powder¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Salt¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Vegetable oil, for basting1 tsp2 tsp1 tbsp4 tsp
Cabbage, sliced, to serve30g60g90g120g
Onion and tomato wedges, to serve20g40g60g80g

Steps

  1. Grind the roasted peanuts fairly fine — this is the base of the yaji spice.
  2. Mix the ground peanuts with the cayenne, paprika, ginger, garlic powder, onion powder, cloves, bouillon powder, and salt until evenly combined.
  3. Toss the sliced beef lightly with a little oil, then thread it onto skewers (soak wooden skewers in water first if using them).
  4. Coat the skewers generously and evenly with the yaji spice mix, pressing it on with your fingers. Let rest at least 15–30 minutes.
  5. Ask an adult to help heat a grill or grill pan to high heat.
  6. Grill the skewers 2–4 minutes per side, basting lightly with oil, until charred at the edges and cooked to your liking.
  7. Sprinkle a little extra yaji spice over the hot skewers right off the grill.
  8. Serve with sliced cabbage, raw onion, and tomato wedges alongside.

Nigerian Groundnut (Peanut) Soup with Chicken

50 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Ground Peanut Paste

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Chicken thighs, bone-in150g300g450g600g
Raw peanuts, toasted and ground (or peanut butter)40g80g120g160g
Red palm oil15ml30ml45ml60ml
Onion, chopped20g40g60g80g
Plum tomato/pepper, blended30g60g90g120g
Scotch bonnet pepper¼½¾1
Fresh ginger, grated½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Garlic clove, minced1234
Stock or water150ml300ml450ml600ml
Fresh spinach, chopped30g60g90g120g
Bouillon cube¼½¾1
Salt¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp

Steps

  1. Season the chicken with a little onion, salt, and the bouillon cube. Ask an adult to help boil it in water to cover until just tender, about 20 minutes. Reserve the stock.
  2. If starting from raw peanuts, toast them in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring constantly, until fragrant, then grind to a rough paste.
  3. Heat the palm oil in a pot, add the onion, and sauté until soft. Stir in the blended tomato, scotch bonnet, ginger, and garlic, and fry 8–10 minutes until thickened.
  4. Stir in the ground peanut paste (or peanut butter), mixing well and loosening it with a splash of reserved stock.
  5. Gradually whisk in the rest of the reserved stock, a little at a time, until smooth with no lumps.
  6. Add the chicken pieces, cover partially, and simmer over low heat 25–30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the soup thickens and a thin layer of oil rises to the surface.
  7. Stir in the chopped spinach and cook 5 more minutes.
  8. Adjust seasoning and serve hot over rice or with a side of fufu.

Waakye

45 min (beans soaked overnight)MediumServes 1–4

Prep — Dried Black-Eyed Peas

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Dried black-eyed peas, soaked overnight40g80g120g160g
Long-grain parboiled rice60g120g180g240g
Dried waakye leaves, or pinch baking sodasmall handfulsmall handful2 handfuls2 handfuls
Water350ml700ml1050ml1400ml
Salt¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Plum tomato/pepper, blended (stew)40g80g120g160g
Onion, chopped (stew)15g30g45g60g
Vegetable oil (stew)10ml20ml30ml40ml
Ripe plantain, sliced½11½2
Oil, for frying plantain15ml30ml45ml60ml
Egg, boiled, to serve1234

Steps

  1. Rinse the soaked black-eyed peas and place them in a pot with the water and the dried waakye leaves (if using).
  2. Bring to a boil, then simmer 40–45 minutes until the beans are tender. Remove and discard the leaves — the liquid should now look reddish-brown. (No leaves? Stir in a small pinch of baking soda instead.)
  3. Rinse the rice and stir it into the pot with the beans. Check the water level, topping up if needed, then season with salt.
  4. Cover and simmer over low heat 20–25 minutes, without stirring too much, until the rice is tender and the water is absorbed.
  5. Meanwhile, make the stew: fry the blended tomato and onion in oil over medium heat 10–12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened. Season with salt.
  6. Ask an adult to help fry the plantain slices in oil over medium heat, about 2–3 minutes per side, until golden and caramelized.
  7. Serve the rice and beans with a spoonful of stew, the fried plantain, a boiled egg, and a sprinkle of gari on the side.

Red Red

40 minEasy-MediumServes 1–4

Prep — Red Palm Oil

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Dried black-eyed peas, soaked (or cooked/canned)60g120g180g240g
Red palm oil20ml40ml60ml80ml
Onion, chopped20g40g60g80g
Plum tomato, blended30g60g90g120g
Scotch bonnet pepper¼½¾1
Fresh ginger, grated¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Garlic clove, minced½11½2
Bouillon cube¼½¾1
Salt¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Ripe plantain½11½2
Oil, for frying plantain15ml30ml45ml60ml

Steps

  1. Cook the soaked black-eyed peas in fresh water with a pinch of salt until tender, about 35–40 minutes (or use drained canned/pre-cooked beans to skip this step). Reserve a little cooking liquid.
  2. Ask an adult to help heat the red palm oil in a pot over medium heat until it turns fluid and fragrant — don't let it smoke.
  3. Add the chopped onion and sauté until soft.
  4. Stir in the blended tomato, scotch bonnet, ginger, and garlic. Fry 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened and the oil starts to separate.
  5. Stir in the cooked beans along with a splash of their cooking liquid. Simmer 10 minutes, seasoning with the bouillon cube and salt.
  6. Meanwhile, fry the plantain slices in oil 2–3 minutes per side until deeply golden and caramelized at the edges.
  7. Serve the bean stew hot with the fried plantain alongside for scooping.

Nigerian Pepper Soup

40 minEasyServes 1–4

Prep — Pepper Soup Spice

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Goat meat or firm white fish, cubed150g300g450g600g
Onion, chopped20g40g60g80g
Fresh ginger, grated½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Garlic clove, minced1234
Scotch bonnet pepper¼½¾1
Nigerian pepper soup spice mix½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Bouillon cube¼½¾1
Water or stock200ml400ml600ml800ml
Scent leaf or fresh basil, chopped5g10g15g20g
Salt¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp

Steps

  1. Season the goat meat with the onion, ginger, garlic, and salt in a pot, then add the water.
  2. Ask an adult to help bring it to a boil, skimming off any foam. Simmer 30–40 minutes until the goat is fork-tender (fish only needs about 10 minutes total, added later).
  3. Stir in the scotch bonnet, pepper soup spice mix, and bouillon cube. Simmer 10 more minutes to let the spices infuse the broth.
  4. Taste and adjust the salt and heat level to your liking.
  5. Stir in the chopped scent leaf just before removing from the heat.
  6. Ladle the hot broth and meat into bowls and serve as is, or with a side of steamed rice.

Chin Chin

30 min (+frying)EasyServes 1–4

Prep — Cutting the Dough

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
All-purpose flour100g200g300g400g
Granulated sugar20g40g60g80g
Butter, softened15g30g45g60g
Milk20ml40ml60ml80ml
Baking powder¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Ground nutmeg¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Saltpinchpinch⅛ tsp¼ tsp
Vegetable oil, for deep-frying500ml500ml750ml1000ml

Steps

  1. In a bowl, whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, nutmeg, and salt together.
  2. Add the softened butter and rub it into the flour with your fingertips until the mixture looks like coarse crumbs.
  3. Gradually add the milk, mixing just until a firm, non-sticky dough comes together. Knead briefly on a floured surface until smooth.
  4. Roll the dough out to about ¼-inch (5mm) thickness.
  5. Cut into strips, then cut crosswise into small squares or diamonds, about ¾-inch (2cm) pieces.
  6. Ask an adult to help heat the oil in a deep, heavy pot to 325–350°F (165–175°C).
  7. Fry the chin chin in small batches (don't crowd the pot) over medium heat, stirring occasionally, 5–8 minutes until deep golden and crunchy all the way through.
  8. Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and let cool completely — they get crunchier as they cool.
